title: Ex-Tabung Haji CEO, CFO claim trail to cheating over RM3.3b hibah payment
text:
Ex-Tabung Haji CEO, CFO claim trial to cheating board to facilitate RM3.3 bil hibah payment Thursday 22 Oct 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Highlight Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 22): Two former senior Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) officials pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here on Thursday for cheating the board of directors in relation to hibah payments totalling RM3.3 billion for the 2017 financial year.
 Former chief executive officer Datuk Seri Johan Abdullah, 70, and former chief financial officer Datuk Rozaida Omar, 63, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial after the single joint charge was read out to them before Judge Norma Ismail. 
 According to the charge sheet sighted by The Edge , the duo allegedly deceived Lembaga Tabung Haji’s board of directors in February 2018 by presenting a working paper proposing adjustments to investment property values. 
 These adjustments were allegedly made to artificially inflate Tabung Haji’s total profit in its unaudited, non-consolidated financial statements for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2017.
 This was done to facilitate the payment of hibah (distribution/bonus) to Lembaga Tabung Haji depositors for financial year 2017 amounting to approximately RM3.3 billion.
 The charge sheet states that through this deception, the duo had induced the board of directors of Tabung Haji to approve the working paper and the property valuation readjustments. 
 “... an act they [the board] would not have performed had they known the true market values of the investment properties and the actual profits of Lembaga Tabung Haji,” the charge sheet read out to the duo. 
 The investment properties involved in the value readjustment include Bangunan TH Platinum Park, Bangunan TH Perdana and Bangunan TH Selborn. 
 The charge, framed under Section 417 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, provides for a maximum jail term of five years, a fine, or both upon conviction.
 Deputy public prosecutors Datuk Nazran Mohd Sham, Rohaiza Abd Rahman and Siti Aina Rodhiah Md Shikh prosecuted.
 Lawyer Shamsul Sulaiman represented Rozaida, while Johan was represented by lawyers Datuk Shukri Mohamed and Malissa Shukri.
 The court granted each accused bail of RM60,000 with one surety and fixed Dec 8 for mention for submission of documents.
